Company Description Diode Labs is an industrial electronics company that delivers integrated hardware and software solutions across embedded firmware, industrial IoT and SCADA systems, EV charging infrastructure, solar power conversion, building automation, and aerospace and defense electronics. The organization operates as a single vertically integrated engineering center, carrying programs from schematic design through firmware development, systems integration, and production. This model reduces integration risk, shortens development timelines, and preserves design intent from concept to deployment. Diode Labs serves as a center of excellence for applied electronics engineering, unifying printed circuit board design, embedded systems, industrial automation, and power electronics under one technical team.
Role Description The Embedded Software Engineer will design, implement, and maintain firmware and embedded software for a range of industrial and IoT systems, working closely with hardware engineers to ensure reliable end-to-end solutions. Day-to-day responsibilities include developing and testing embedded software, performing debugging and root-cause analysis, optimizing performance and reliability, and contributing to software architecture and design decisions. The engineer will participate in code reviews, create technical documentation, and support system integration and validation across production and field environments. This is a full-time remote role, requiring effective collaboration with distributed team members and proactive communication across disciplines.
Qualifications
Strong skills in Embedded Software Programming and Embedded Software development for real-time and resource-constrained systems.
Experience in general Software Development and Software Design, including architecture, modular design, and code maintainability.
Proficiency in Debugging embedded systems, using tools such as logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, debuggers, and protocol analyzers.
Hands-on experience with C/C++ (or similar languages) for embedded targets, microcontrollers, and RTOS-based systems.
Familiarity with hardware–software integration, communication protocols (e.g., SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet), and industrial or IoT systems.
Ability to read and understand schematics and work effectively with hardware engineering teams.
Strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and ability to work independently in a remote, cross-functional environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
Experience with version control (e.g., Git), continuous integration, and collaborative development workflows is beneficial.
Background in industrial automation, power electronics, or aerospace and defense systems is a plus.

At 20:05 UTC on October 29, approximately USD 6.36 billion began moving out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes. It is the largest crypto theft on record, roughly four times the Bybit hack of February 2025.

TRM Labs attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite state-sponsored hacking unit, based on robust on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The same group was named by the FBI in the Bybit hack, and the staging, the Tornado Cash funding and the pre-signed transactions all match earlier North Korea-linked heists.

The response has been fast. Tether, Circle, Ripple, World Liberty Financial and Arbitrum’s Security Council have frozen roughly USD 2.7 billion. But the attacker still controls about USD 2.4 billion in assets beyond any issuer’s reach, and is racing to convert and move them.

TRM continues to work with Binance and the Beacon Network to track the funds and alert partners in real time. The story is still developing, and we will share more as the investigation unfolds.
